MCF PROJECT DIRECTOR'S 2019 FIRST QUARTER REPORT

1. INTRODUCTION

In 2018 many of the planned activities for the Managalas Conservation Area was not implemented
due to various reasons including the late approval and transfer of funds by the main donor of the
project Rainforest Foundation Norway (RFN) through Partners with Melanesia (PwM), the
holder of the project and implementing partner. The Conservation was gazetted and officially
declared in 2017 so there were a lot of expectation from the local communities/landowners
especially support for sustainable livelihood activities which is the main purpose for the funding
from RFN apart from the conservation objective. Also there were a lot of issues on this discussed
and decisions taken at the District Wide Combine Forum held in November at Yoivi village in
Zone 8. Therefore, the hope was some of these main planned activities will be undertaken in the
early part of the year because of the up-coming Local Level Government Elections in the second
quarter of the year. However, there was delays gain due to late transfer of funds by RFN because
of the delays with audit report. This report is record of activities in the first quarter of the year
which is from January to March 2019.

2. ACTIVITIES UNDERTAKEN IN THE QUARTER.

2.1 Follow-up on Financial Reports/Acquittals

Last year PwM transferred K59,000 to MCF account for its capacity building activities and
because the Finance Officer was new I worked with him to ensure that all acquittals of the funds
transferred were done to meet the audit requirements as stringent requirements were put in place
in the contract for this. Also the amount of K+1,000 was not transferred which affected payment
for services and MCF staff and CBO allowances and this remains major concern and issue where
staff wanted to boycott planned activities for the year. | also discussed the reporting requirements
and the financial management guidelines with the Finance Officer to ensure that he was well
versed with the financial reporting requirements

2.1. Follow-up Work on the Establishment of Managalas Conservation Area

Management Commiittee.
The District Wide Combine Forum held at Yoivi village in zone 8 last November approved the
landowner representatives on the Managalas Conservation Area Management Committee
(MCAMC) as required under the Conservation Areas Act. Therefore, armed with this decision, |
liased and worked with both PwM and Officers from the Sustainable Environment Protection
Division of the Conservation Environment Protection Authority (CEPA) to formally establish the
MCAMC as required under Section 25 of the Conservation Areas Act as the committee plays an
important role in overseen the management of the conservation area including approving the
management plan, making rules/by-laws for the conservation area and supervising the work of

=== page 8 ===
rangers. These including writing letters. sending emails and holding one on one meetings with
relevant officers about establishment of the committee and funding for work of the committee.

2.2 Follow-up on Ministers Funding Commitment.

A lot of my time in the quarter was spent on following up on the commitment made by the Minister
for Environment & Conservation, Hon. John Pundari during launching of the Conservation Area at
Itokama on 29 November 2017. This was to assist the local communities/landowners with
sustainable livelihood alternatives especially marketing of coffee so I wanted to ensure that the
funding was released to MCF before the season proper starts for the coffee. Our plan was to give
the funds equally to each coffee growing zones accessible to markets to arrange for group
marketing of coffee from their zones organised by the partner Community Based Organisations
(CBOs). These including sending letters, follow-up emails and one on ne meetings with the CEPA
Managing Director and relevant Officers with CEPA's SEP Division. It was a frustrating effort as
this was continuing from 2019 after the submission of the necessary supporting documentation to
the CEPA Managing Director as requested by him.

2.3 Proposal and Budget to UNDP/CEPA GEF 5 Project for the
Managaias Conservation Area Buffer Zone Support Project.

Upon request by the GEF 5 Project Management Unit (PMU) housed within UNDP I developed a
proposal for the Managalas Conservation Area and Buffer Zone Support Project to cover costs for
establishing the MCAMC, selection and training of Rangers and support equipment and costs,
sustainable livelihood alternatives in line with the Protected Area Policy and education awareness
programme especially targeting schools in the area. They also asked me do develop a budget for the
MCAMC to cover its costs which I did and submitted to them and CEPA. The plan was to have the
proposal considered by the Project Board/Steering Committee at the planned Board meeting in
May, This was to meet some of the funding constraints for implementation of planned activities.

2.4 Meetings with Governor for Gro for Funding Assistance.

A number of meetings were held with the Governor for Oro, Hon. Garry Juffa including follow-up
letters and emails about the funding commitment by the Governor for activities in the conservation
area including establishment of the Council of Chiefs and the Community Leaders Summit. [ also
followed up with the Officers in the Governor's Office for this funding as these were also activities
agreed to at the District Wide Combine Forum in Zone 8 last November. The main issue according
to Governor Juffa is the late release of funds by the Finance Department so he told me to continue
with the follow-ups so that the funding committed can be released for the planned activities..

2.5 MCF Board Matters.

There has been problem with having the regular board meetings because of funding constraints and
also the board decisions have to be implemented so I have been in regular contact with the
Chairman who is in Popondetta due to his medical condition to update him on board matters. There
are important matters including funding, implementation of activities , staff matters and networking
with relevant Provincial and District Officers as well as management of the project vehicle that the
Chairman and other board members needed to be up-dated on so it is important for the regular
communication or one on one meetings when I am in the Province.

2

=== page 9 ===
2.6 Arrangement for Management of the Project Venicie.

The vehicle donated by New Britain Palm Oi! which was parked at the Oro Guest House for a
number of years was eventually serviced by the company mechanics and registered with MVIL last
year. This has assisted with easing some of the transport problems faced for implementation of
planned activities. However, because of the bad road condition it needed to managed and driven by
a reliable driver to serve its purpose. A committee of the board was established to manage the
vehicle including supervision of the driver as per board decision last November. This arrangement
was to be assessed to see if it was working out, if not to make changes to the arrangement.
Therefore, I was in constant communication with the Chairman and the MCF staff regarding the
management of the vehicle.

2.7. Other Administrative Matters

1 also developed reporting formats for MCF and CBO staff which will be presented at the planning
meeting before they can be finalised. I also ensured at that each MCF staff have proper
identification cards and that the MCF office in Popondetta is properly maintained by the Finance
and Admin. Officer.

3. PROBLEMS, ISSUES/CHALLENGES.

Some of the obvious problems and challenges have been funding constraints to implement planned
activities, communication problems, bad road condition and the main issue with commitment by
MCF staff because of the non-payment of allowances. The late release of funds earmarked for
capacity building activities by PwM has also contributed to some of these difficulties.

A lot of stakeholders including business groups, cooperatives, associations, women and youth
groups as well as schools are requesting for funding assistance for their own planned activities but
MCF being a small organisation with no funding base is unable to meet their request thus, creating
frustrations. There is for MCF to carry out awareness on its roles and functions as per its
constitution and the need to have the membership arrangement in place so that there is broad
representation on the board to assist with the work of the organisation.

4, FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS

There are number of urgent matters that need to be followed up including the funding commitment
by the Minister, the proposal to the UNDP/CEPA GEF 5 Project, establishment of the MCAMC
and funding commitment by the Oro Governor. The other activities are mainly administrative
matters including contracts for staff, organising the planning and board meetings and supervision of
the Finance and Admin. Officer to improve on the financial reports for MCF.

5. CONCLUSION

In conclusion, I can say that there are a lot of expectation of local communities/landowners and
stakeholders in the conservation area especially schools for funding and other support since the
declaration of the Conservation Area. MCF is unable to meet these expectations because of funding
constraints and other challenges including lack of support from stakeholders like the Afore LLG,
Oro Provincial and Ijivitari District Administration and line national agencies especially CEPA and
CCDA. Coupled with this is the problem of MCF staff not having the confidence to follow-up with
3

=== page 10 ===
Provincial Authorities to support the activities in the area. The main issue of MCF having its own
audit report needs to be addressed as this is affecting MCF’s ability to raise its own funding from
donors because the production of an external audit report is one major requirement by donors.

The need to have the MCAMC established and in place and properly funded to carry out its
functions provided for by law is a priority. CEPA Officer needs to constantly reminded of their
roles and the work of MCF as a local partner in implementing the Protected Area Policy and
relevant legislations especially the Conservation Areas Act. Also there is need to have MOU’'s
signed with Afore LLG, the Ijivitari District Administration and Oro Provincial Administration for
assistance with the implementation of planned activities and especially for aligning the
Conservation Area Management Plans with the plans of each of the various levels of government in
the province.

Respectfully Submitted,

Damien Ase
Project Director

Introduction:

Planning is very vital for every organisation's and individual person to achieve their goals
or dreams. In order to achieve that goal and dream, you have to make plan to know how
much time and resources will be required to achieve it with given deadlines. Therefore
Partners with Melanesians is guided by its work plan to work towards achieving its goals,
purpose, vision & mission. Plans can be changed and revised as time goes by to allow for
improvement or alterations due to the surrounding circumstances along the way.

Partners with Melanesians annually has two planning workshop in February and June
respectively. This year 2019, we had the first planning workshop at PNG Bible Translation
Association, Waigani from the 8° — 12* of April 2019.

1. Give a short and to the point description of the project that you are applying for (max
0.5 pages)

A. Proposed Managalas Conservation Area Project
Partners With Melanesians Inc. has been working with the people of the Managalas
Plateau, Ijivitari District, of the Oro Province for over two decades to protect the
360,000 hectares of rainforest, its habitants numbering over 20,000 and its natural
resources. Community mobilization and consensus building formed the cornerstone of
PWM’s mission in strengthening the traditional decision making processes, where the
communities voices are collectively echoed as one through the district wide combine
forums. The forums provided the platform to sortout miss-understandings, confusions,
conflicts and differences and to ensure peace, understanding, unity, stability and
cooperation is maintained amongst them as they continue to define their purpose.
The idea of protecting the Managalas Plateau was conceived much later, after
communities were organized, mobilized and made aware of the importance of several
important species of flora and fauna thought to be endemic to the area, one of which is
the Queen Alexandria Bird-wing Butterfly.

Additionally, due to the vastness and difficult terrain of the area, the 360,000 hectares of
landmass was divided into ten small clusters, made up of several clan groups, known as

=== page 2 ===
Multiple year application form:2018-2022

cultural zones, based on langauge grouping, kinship and family tics. Originally, those
clustered groups were convenicatly assembled for the purposes of building consensus
among clan groups, however, as it later turned out, these structures made management
of clan lands easily accessible for the participatory land use management planning in
Getermining the various uses of their land. Upon demacating the clan lands, sustainabic
livelihood alternative projects such as honcy bee farming, rice cultivation, subsistence
potato farming, organic coffee farming, amongst others, were encouraged on the
atlocated plots and proved to be sucessful, eventually providing alternative income for
the local communities.

The zones then formed community based-organizations (CBOs) and were formally
registered with the Investment Promotion Authority whose main purpose was to
management affairs of the cultural zones by raising income to support clan initiatives,
while sustainably managing the resources in the conservation area in the respective
zones, An umbrella organization, the Managaias Conservation Foundation, previousty
called Managalas Development Foundation (MDF) was set-up to coordinate and ensure
efficient performance and management of those CBO, after the arca becomes a
nationally declared conservation arca.

On the 8th of November 2012, PWM submitted an application to the Minister for
Environment and Conservation and CEPA for consideration uader the Conservation
Areas Act (1978) for processing for the next CA. After waiting for four years for all the

it finally went before the PNG National Execative Council (NEC) in 2016. On
the 15th of December 2016, NEC approved the PWM application by way of NEC
Decision No. 325/2016. The NEC decision will be effected for formality and legal status
through the National Gazcttal by the NEC Secretariat and CEPA after getting the
instruments drafted and sigace by the Head of State, HE Governor Genera! of PNG,
PWM is now awaiting that process and while waiting for the gazettal, PWM and the
loca! partacrs are preparing for the activities after gazcttal with the on-site declaration
to be on the Mamazaias plateau at Itckaimea,

For PWM, the challenge row is to cnsure that the Managalas Conservetion
Foundation’s (MCF) capacity is fully enbanced sand MCF made ready to take on the
huge task of managing the 360,000 hectares land, with 11 CBOs and over 20,000 peopie
in PNG’s second conservation. Additionally, the task beyong 2018 for PWM is to
consolidate the work with MCF in puttiug in place a Comservation Area Management
Committee to ensure the management and sustainability of the conservation area, and to
come up with a Conservation Area Management Plan and Strategies to guide tue
conservation efforts.

PWM will continue to facilitate and link MCF and its CBOs to other partners including
the respective government agencies who are able to support and ensure sustainable
development options are realised for the local communities as they continuc to conserve,
manage and utilise their natural resources for their livelihood for now and their future
generations.

3B. Inaina Wildlife Management Area Project
It began as an initiative of a visionary Clan Leader in opposing 2 scam SABL operation
for industrial large scale logging in the area and on their clan land measuring 9,712.20

=== page 3 ===
Multiple year application form:201 8-2022

hectares. The Fagagara clan from Inaina in the Kairuku Hiri District of Central
Province, approached DEC/CEPA and DCD for REDD+ projects and eventually, CEPA
invited PWM to be a partner in 2011 in what was a mere call for support in stopping the
logging operations. After successfully halting the logging operations, the success story
was an opportunity for concrete conservation efforts in protecting the arca from the
dangers of logging and other Industrial developments including Oil Palm. Guided by the
‘Flora and Fauna Protection Act’ PWM began the community consultation process,
mobilizing and creating awareness on environment protection and biodiversity
conservation as opposed to industrial, large-scale developments. In exactly five (5) years
of PWM’s involvement, Inaina was declared as a Wildlife Management Area (WMA) on
the 23° March 2017, after having passed all the requirements set by the government's
Conservation Environment Protection Authority (CEPA) in accordance with the ‘Flora
and Fauna Protection Act’.

PWM is now working with the local communities to put in place a WMA Management
Plan and s WMA Management Committee to oversee the management of the WMA,
while at the same time, assisting to set up a focal body to coordinate conservation efforts
and alternative income generation options in the WMA. The capacity of the local focal
body is at this stage is paramount as ongoing plans are in place. Simultancousiy, PWM
is mindful that the WMA status will lapse in 5 years, thas PWM. ts engaging in dialogue
with CEPA to ensure the WMA or whatever form of conservation status under the New
Protected Area Policy of Government, remains true for the people of Inaina and their
future generations so that PWM’s efforts from 2011 to now is not wasted. In addition,
other clan and nearby communities are expressing interest to extend the WMA
boundaries so they can be included so this gives the local CBO (Fagagara Development
Foundation Inc.) and PWM to initiate the process with CEPA for these clans and nearby
communities to be included and the current WMA area with their land areas as
extensions to the current WMA boundary and over the next five (5) year, it can be
developed into a bigger conservation area under Protected Ares Policy. It is also in the
plans of PWM that, Insina WMA with its close proximity to Port Moresby, with pristine
unlogged rainforest and biodiversity with clean fresh water and lots of birdlife, the area
will be converted inte a Ecotourism bub and Rainforest Education Ceatre with
conference facilities and other facilities, so that the Centre and Spin-of activities can
financially support the management of the WMA and provide opportunities for local
employment and this can further the motivation of the local communities to ensure
protection and conservation of the WMA is maintained.

C. Proposed Mt. Karimui Conservation Area Project
The Propose Mt. Karimul Conservation Area Project was a community initiative,
established in 2006 and 2007 with the support from another national NGO called
Conservation Melanesians Inc. (CM). However CM did not continue duc to financial
constraints so locals from the area approached PWM with their strategic plan and
sought assistance to support the conservation objective. Hence, work in the proposed
Mt. Karimui Conservation Area Project began with the signing of a tri-partite
memorandum of understanding (MOU) in 2011, between the local communities, the
local level government, the Simbu Provincial Government, and Partners With
Melanesians Inc,
Ideally located between the borders of Simbu, Eastern Highlands, Southern Highlands,
Gulf, Jiwaka and Western Highlands Provinces, the 160,000 hectares of fertile land is

\

=== page 4 ===
Muhtipte year application form:201 8-2022

geographically isolated, yct rich in biodiversity, boasting some exotic specics of flora &
fauna,

Amidst the chalienges of a growing population, the locais are determined in addressing
these social issues while sustainably managing ane utilizing their environment and
natural resources. As the arca around them is developing, the need for increased energy
use has compelled the government to explore opportunities in hydropower generation
using the main Waghi river that runs through Tua river, within the conservation ares
and passes Karimui Station on the northern side Mowing down to Kikori through Wabo
emptying into the Guif of Papua. Additionaily, as part of the National Government’s
V2050 Plans and the Economic Corridor Plans, it is planning to link up Karimu! with
the surrounding provinces through the construction of a national highway to link with
the existing Sir Okuk Highway, and that will expose the conservation arca.

Whilst these are unevoidable development plans, PWM and the local communities
through its local Community Based Organization called Karimui Conservation and
Resource Management Programme Inc. (KCRMPI) are seriously taking into
consideration these development pians and are considering plans on how to ensure these
developments do not disturb the conservation effort by working closely with the
Government fo ensure things are done in the most appropriate and environmentally
friendly manner.

Nevertheless, PWM is continuing its efforts in raising awareness on biodiversity
conservation and cross-cutting issues like population, water and sanitation, gender
empowerment etc. while encouraging the consensus building processes in decision
making on the utilization of resources within the conservation arca. PWM is also
assisting with buiiding the capacity of the Karimui Conservation and Resource
Management Programme Inc. (KCRMPD), to enable sound management of the
conservation area, as well as linking the area with cxternal markets especially on
organic coffee and other income generating food crops like peanuts and spices.

2018 and beyond, PWM will be concentrating its conservation efforts in preparing the
area for the conservation area status with the establishment of a conservation area
management plan and committee, and roager trainings, while at the same time, ensuring
that all externai boundaries are mapped and a rapid biodiversity assessment carried ont
to measure against the bascline, with the aim of establishing a research station for
studies on the exotic flora and fauna in the conservation arca.

D. Proposed Collinwood Bay Conservation Area Project
Initial community and stakeholder consultation were conducted in 2015, late 2016 and
early 2017 with this constal and injand community of the Collinwood Bay, Ijivitari
District of the Oro Province, with the aim of reviving conservation efforts initially
carried out by a now defunct national NGC conservation organization, Conservation
Melanesia. This community is not new to conservation work. Similar efforts were
carried out over 10 years, however, duc to operational and management challenges
faced by Conservation Melanesia, it affected plans and work programs in CWB,
resulting in the closure of the operations.

Simultaneously, after 20 plus years of struggling to put an eud to a lengthy court battle
with a logging company, the locais finally won the court case in 2014, ending years of

Sy

=== page 5 ===
Multiple year pplication form:2018-2022

destructive logging to their forests that also subsequently destroyed the marine life that
supports the coastal communities who are dependent on the marine resources for food
and sustenance.

The locals have seen and felt the negative effects of large scale development to their
environment and have opted for conservation and sustainable development options. The
area encompasses a total of 9 customary tribal groups. During the consultation work of
PWM between 2016/2017, the 9 tribes of CWB saw the need and importance of giving
recognition and uphold the status of women in CWB as equal and created the Women’s
platform for engagement as the 10” tribe and for the voice of all women. There are 326
clans, and 25 bamicts that spreads over 560,00€+ hectares of delta plains, lowland and
mid-montane rainforest and savannah grassland and is geographically challenging in
terms of reaching out to all these communities, Additionally, the entire CWB traditional
and customary practices have no particular definition for gender equality in that women
are not part of any decision making process and are often not considered as important.
While the chief is the ultimate head of the clan and he has the fina) say, but is done in
consultation and through consensus, The definition of consensus in CWB is absolute;
there fs no consensus if one person, one clan or one tribe is not in agreement to a
decision. A number of dialects are spoken throughout the area while English is
commonly spoken and understood amongst the 20,500+ population. Like all other rural
isolated communities in PNG, the Collinwood Bay area receives very little government
services which are limited to basis health and education while they depend heavily on
their environment for food, water, building materials and other environmental goods
and services.

PWM is now gearing up on creating awareness on issues that are affecting the
environment like climate change and its impact on water and food security. Whilst this
will be an on-going program, PWM will be liaising with the local communities in
identifying a focal community based organization to coordinate work on the ground,
through which a memorandum of understanding will be established in defining a clear
working relationship and partnership between all important stakeholders including the
focal communities and their community based organization, the local level government
and the provincial government, in identifying ways to assist the communities in
conserving their environment while managing and utilizing their forest and marine
resources for their livelihoods. This arrangement will ensure all key stakeholders will be
meaningfully engaged in ensuring critical enablers like effective leadership and good
governance, environmental legislations and policies, performance and accountability etc.
are in place for achieving successful conservation outcomes and sustainable livelihoods.

The Managalas Conservation Foundation inc. (MCF) need to have intuitive leadership

What is the current situation?

PWM conducted the stakeholder and community consultation in 2015, late 2016 and

Conservation Area Project in the Oro Province. The other achievement was the
declaration and launching of the Inaina Wildlife Management Area in the Central

a) Geographical location:

Both the Proposed Managalas Conservation Area Project (MCAP) and the Proposed
Collinwood Bay Conservation Area (CBCA) are in the ljivitari District of the Oro
Province. The MCAP is a terrestrial project in that it is in the interior of the province, at
the Afore Local Level Government and is accessible by 4x4 Toyota Land cruiser on a 4
hours’ drive on unsealed graveled road and light aircraft. The current population of the
Managalas Area according to 2011 census is 21,000+. Meanwhile the CBCA is both a
terrestrial and marine project. It is in the Tufi LLG and is also remote from urban
township of Popondetta. It is only accessible by sea and light aircraft. With a current
population of 10,500+ people, most villages are scattered and the ragged terrain remains
a challenge for communications and patrols.

The Inaina area is in the Kairnku Hiri District of Central Province. PNG’s capital city
of Port Moresby is 3 hours drive to Inaina. This is a small aren of approximately
9,721.20 hectares with about 350 people.

The Mt. Karimui area is located between the Simbu, Eastern Highlands, Gulf, Jiwaka
and Southern Highlands provinces, The area is isolated and remote from the rest of the
country and is currently accessible only by light aircraft. The Mt. Karimui Conservation
Area Project covers a land area of 160,000 hectares and has a total population of 16,
000,
